title: workspace-sync status.json clobber — investigate the 2026-07-10 00:0x-window mini-incident (poller commit 25a79b0 references phantom SHA a88d026 as the culprit), assess whether the workspace-owned surface needs protection analogous to PROP-127 CHECK 3 (sentinel-file reversion), or whether the clobber class is best left to poller's self-heal.

context.why_now: Poller commit 25a79b0 (2026-07-10T00:14:37Z, message 'poller: 2026-07-10T00:09Z poll — net quiet, PRED-FIELD-2026Q2 d=10 (HIGH heartbeat), PRED-073 d=40 (terminal heartbeat); restores status.json fields after workspace-sync clobber incident (a88d026)') explicitly cites a workspace-sync clobber of status.json fields that poller had to self-heal. The referenced SHA a88d026 is NOT findable in current git history (either rebased away, force-pushed over, or the SHA in the message is truncated/mistyped). status.json is workspace-owned per CLAUDE.md OWNERSHIP, so PROP-127 CHECK 3 (which protects SENTINEL_FILES = 9 canonical git-owned files) would not have caught this by design. But 'workspace-sync improvised the sync path and clobbered a workspace-owned file such that a downstream agent had to self-heal' is the same behavioral class as the 2026-07-07 4a5b8115 incident that PROP-127 addressed for git-owned files. Question: should the workspace-owned surface get its own protective mechanism, or is the ~30-day cadence of this class of incident + downstream self-heal sufficient?

evidence_pointers.workspace_sync_run_that_probably_did_it: 72aa269 (2026-07-10T00:08:08Z, 'Workspace sync: 2026-07-10T00:08:08Z' — the cycle immediately preceding poller's restore). Modified curmudgeon/latest-verify-summary.txt + closed-issues.json + narrative-cite-audit sentinel — 3 files. status.json not visibly in the file list at the top level but a diff-inspection of the commit would confirm whether status.json fields were touched via a sneak edit or if the clobber was in a different neighboring cycle.
evidence_pointers.phantom_sha_a88d026: Not findable via git log --all in the current clone. Possibilities: (a) truncated SHA prefix (poller may have written a hash prefix that no longer matches after a subsequent history change); (b) rebased-away commit (unlikely — workspace-sync clones fresh and pushes normally; no rebase in the flow); (c) typo in poller's message string. Not blocking — the point is that poller detected AND fixed a status.json regression, so the incident is real regardless of which upstream commit caused it.

prior_related.PROP-127: sentinel-file byte-reversion CHECK 3 — protects 9 git-owned files against pre-push byte-reversion. Would NOT have caught status.json because status.json is workspace-owned (only workspace-sync writes it FUSE→git).
prior_related.DIRECTIVE-20260709-001: workspace-sync 4a5b8115 multi-file reversion — root cause was workspace-sync improvisation (skipped smart_copy, pushed stale FUSE view). Same behavioral class likely applies here.
prior_related.poller_prompt: monitor/prompts/poller.md — poller's built-in status.json field restoration mechanism is a durable self-heal, but relies on poller running WITHIN a window after the clobber. Timeline: workspace-sync 00:08 → poller 00:14 = 6 minutes. Poller's own scheduled cadence is daily, so this happens to be one of the moments-per-day poller can catch a fresh clobber. If workspace-sync clobbered status.json at, say, 04:08 UTC (its most common cadence slot), poller wouldn't run until ~24h later — much longer stale window.

questions_to_answer: Q1 — Confirm the culprit workspace-sync commit that clobbered status.json. Was it 72aa269 (00:08), or a different neighboring cycle (04:08, 08:08, 12:08)? git diff the working tree of status.json across the workspace-sync cycles on 2026-07-10 to identify which cycle wrote the stale content.
Q2 — What FIELDS in status.json got clobbered? Poller's message says 'restores status.json fields' plural — enumerate them from the diff to understand the impact class.

Q3 — Was this the same improvisation-path signature as 4a5b8115 (skips_total=0 while neighbors had 1,169+ skips)? Check the workspace-sync run report for the identified culprit cycle and compare its skips_total to neighboring cycles.
part_A_forensic_confirmation.output: monitor/tinker/reports/workspace-sync-status-json-clobber-2026-07-10.md — one-page report answering Q1-Q3 with commit + report SHAs.

candidates_to_evaluate.label: Extend PROP-127 CHECK 3 SENTINEL_FILES to include workspace-owned files (status.json, review-state.json, latest-*-summary.txt)
candidates_to_evaluate.notes: Simplest technical fit. But: workspace-owned files LEGITIMATELY get overwritten by workspace-sync every cycle (that's the whole point). CHECK 3 blocks BYTE-REVERSIONS to historic commit content — for a monotonically-evolving workspace-owned file, that shouldn't trip for legitimate updates. If it does, the fail-open discipline catches it. Worth evaluating: does status.json evolve monotonically enough that byte-reversion would be a valid signal?

candidates_to_evaluate.label: Add pre-push hook CHECK 4: workspace-owned drift semantic check
candidates_to_evaluate.notes: Different mechanism from CHECK 3. Instead of byte-reversion, walk fields of specific workspace-owned files (status.json fields, review-state.json fields) and compare against last commit's values. If a field got zeroed or reverted to a much older value without a corresponding decider/agent commit that ATTRIBUTED the field change, block. More complex, more targeted, more prone to false positives.

candidates_to_evaluate.label: Rely on downstream self-heal (poller, decider) as the protection layer
candidates_to_evaluate.notes: Do nothing. Poller already caught this one. Decider re-writes status.json on every run. Analyst re-writes review-state.json. Steady state: any workspace-sync clobber gets healed within one downstream agent cycle. Cost: transient staleness (minutes to hours) for readers of the workspace-owned files during the window between clobber and heal.

candidates_to_evaluate.label: Move status.json to git-owned classification
candidates_to_evaluate.notes: Reclassifies the file. Then workspace-sync NEVER pushes it and the clobber class disappears. But status.json is written by MANY agents (poller updates poll counters; decider updates prev_decider_run; analyst updates review_state; etc.) — moving to git-owned means every agent writes from clone, not from FUSE. Big refactor. Probably not worth it for one file.

candidates_to_evaluate.label: Instrument workspace-sync's own logic to detect its own improvisation
candidates_to_evaluate.notes: PROP-128-like semantic canary but for workspace-sync itself. If a workspace-sync run's skips_total is 0 while the running average is ~1,000, log a WARN sentinel. Doesn't PREVENT the clobber but SURFACES the class earlier. Could feed integrity's daily audit.

part_B_protection_options_inventory.output: 5-row feasibility table appended to Part A report.

part_C_recommendation.ask: One clear recommendation. Explicitly acceptable outcome: 'OPT-3 (rely on downstream self-heal). Frequency of the clobber class + fast self-heal + high false-positive risk of the alternatives makes protection not worth building.' Operator does not require a fix if the investigation shows the current state is fine.
part_C_recommendation.output: One-paragraph recommendation at the top of the Part A report.

deliverable_acceptance_criteria: If recommendation is a code change (OPT-1, OPT-2, or OPT-5), a follow-up PROP with verification pattern grade B.

constraints.prop_051_disaster_class_review_required: Any protection option that changes workspace-sync's push behavior (OPT-1, OPT-2) must pass PROP-051-class review: fail-open discipline (bug degrades to status quo, not blocking all syncs). PROP-127 established the pattern.
constraints.do_not_pause_agents_during_investigation: Do NOT pause dome-workspace-sync or dome-poller during investigation. This class of incident is rare and self-heals; investigation shouldn't degrade steady-state operation.
